## AuthProvider  mcp/src/auth-provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Supplies bearer tokens to an MCP HTTP transport and may refresh them after a 401 response. */
export interface AuthProvider {
	/**
	 * Token for the next request. May refresh it over the network first, so the transport calls it only
	 * before requests whose answer it waits for. Closing a session reuses the token of the last request.
	 */
	token(): Promise<string | undefined>;
	onUnauthorized?(context: UnauthorizedContext): Promise<void>;
}

## McpFetch  mcp/src/auth-provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type McpFetch = (input: string | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

## UnauthorizedContext  mcp/src/auth-provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface UnauthorizedContext {
	/** The 401 response, or a 403 response whose challenge reports `insufficient_scope`. */
	response: Response;
	serverUrl: URL;
	fetch: McpFetch;
	/** Access token the rejected request carried, if any. A different current token means another request already refreshed it. */
	token?: string;
}

## McpClient  mcp/src/client.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export class McpClient {
	readonly options: Readonly<McpClientOptions>
	constructor(options: McpClientOptions)
	get connectionState(): ClientState
	get serverInfo(): Implementation | undefined
	get serverCapabilities(): ServerCapabilities | undefined
	get instructions(): string | undefined
	get protocolVersion(): string | undefined
	async connect(transport: McpTransport): Promise<InitializeResult>
	request<Result = unknown>(
		method: string,
		params?: Record<string, unknown>,
		options: McpRequestOptions = {},
	): Promise<Result>
	notify(method: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>
	setRequestHandler(method: string, handler: RequestHandler): () => void
	onNotification(method: string, listener: NotificationListener): () => void
	onError(listener: ErrorListener): () => void
	/** Called once when the connection closes, whether the transport dropped or `close()` was called. */
	onClose(listener: CloseListener): () => void
	async ping(options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<void>
	async listTools(options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<Tool[]>
	/** Every resource, following `nextCursor` through all pages. */
	async listResources(options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<Resource[]>
	/** One page of resources, starting at `cursor`. */
	async listResourcesPage(cursor?: string, options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<ListResourcesResult>
	/** Every resource template, following `nextCursor` through all pages. */
	async listResourceTemplates(options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<ResourceTemplate[]>
	/** One page of resource templates, starting at `cursor`. */
	async listResourceTemplatesPage(
		cursor?: string,
		options: McpRequestOptions = {},
	): Promise<ListResourceTemplatesResult>
	async readResource(uri: string, options: McpRequestOptions = {}): Promise<ReadResourceResult>
	async callTool(
		name: string,
		args?: Record<string, unknown>,
		options: McpRequestOptions = {},
	): Promise<CallToolResult>
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## isMcpServerOverride  mcp/src/config.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Whether an entry overrides a server defined elsewhere instead of defining one: it has no `command`,
 * `url` or `type`. Applications let a less trusted file (a project's) override a few fields, such as
 * `enabled`, of a server a trusted file defines; which fields is theirs to decide.
 */
export function isMcpServerOverride(entry: Record<string, unknown>): boolean

## McpHttpServerConfig  mcp/src/config.ts

/** A server reached over Streamable HTTP. */
export interface McpHttpServerConfig extends McpServerConfigBase {

## McpOAuthConfig  mcp/src/config.ts
used by: mcp-effect; evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput
/** OAuth client settings for servers that do not support dynamic client registration. */
export interface McpOAuthConfig {
	/** Pre-registered client id. Without it, the application registers a client with the authorization server. */
	clientId?: string;
	/** As configured; the application decides whether it may reference variables. */
	clientSecret?: string;
	/**
	 * Port of the loopback callback server, for clients registered with a fixed redirect URI. Without
	 * `callbackUrl`, the redirect URI is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`.
	 */
	callbackPort?: number;
	/**
	 * Redirect URI registered for `clientId`, for example `http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback`. It must
	 * be an `http` URI on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`. Without a port, the callback server
	 * listens on `callbackPort` or a free port, which is added to the URI (RFC 8252).
	 */
	callbackUrl?: string;
	/** Scopes to request, separated by spaces. Default: the scopes the server advertises. */
	scope?: string;
	/** `client_name` sent with dynamic client registration. Default: the application's name. */
	clientName?: string;
	/**
	 * How the application identifies itself without `clientId`. `auto` (default): its Client ID Metadata
	 * Document when the authorization server supports them for public clients, otherwise dynamic client
	 * registration. `cimd`: always the document, and sign-in fails without support. `dcr`: always
	 * dynamic client registration.
	 */
	clientRegistration?: "auto" | "dcr" | "cimd";
	/**
	 * Authorization server metadata document (RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect discovery) to use instead of
	 * discovery through the server, for servers that advertise a wrong authorization server or none.
	 * The document is trusted as configured. Must use https, except on loopback hosts.
	 */
	authServerMetadataUrl?: string;
}

## McpServerConfig  mcp/src/config.ts

/** One entry of the `mcpServers` shape: a stdio or a Streamable HTTP server. */
export type McpServerConfig = McpStdioServerConfig | McpHttpServerConfig;

## McpServerConfigBase  mcp/src/config.ts
used by: evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput, mcp-effect via McpHttpServerConfig
/**
 * The `mcpServers` configuration shape that MCP clients share, so configurations can be copied between
 * them: stdio servers (`command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`), Streamable HTTP servers (`url`, `headers`,
 * `oauth`), and `enabled`, `description` and `timeout` for both.
 *
 * ```json
 * {
 *   "mcpServers": {
 *     "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."] },
 *     "docs": { "url": "https://example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}" } }
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * Applications add fields of their own: {@link validateMcpServerConfig} keeps fields it does not know
 * for the caller to check afterwards.
 */

/** Fields every server entry may have. */
interface McpServerConfigBase {
	/** What the server offers, in a sentence. */
	description?: string;
	/** Set to false to keep the entry without connecting. Default: true. */
	enabled?: boolean;
	/** Per-request timeout in seconds. */
	timeout?: number;
}

## McpServerConfigOptions  mcp/src/config.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** What the application adds to the validation of server entries. */
export interface McpServerConfigOptions {
	/**
	 * Checks the `oauth.callbackUrl` (undefined: none configured) of an entry with
	 * `oauth.clientRegistration: "cimd"`: the application's Client ID Metadata Documents must list it.
	 * Returns an error message. Without this check, `"cimd"` is refused.
	 */
	checkMetadataDocumentCallback?(callbackUrl: string | undefined): string | undefined;
}

## McpServerConfigResult  mcp/src/config.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * A validated server entry, tagged with its transport, or why it is invalid. The config is the entry
 * as given: fields the validator does not know are kept, unchecked, for the caller to check.
 */
export type McpServerConfigResult =
	| { kind: "stdio"; config: McpStdioServerConfig & Record<string, unknown> }
	| { kind: "http"; config: McpHttpServerConfig & Record<string, unknown> }
	| { kind: "invalid"; error: string };

}

## createMcpToolName  mcp/src/naming.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, sanitized and shortened with a hash suffix when too long. Like Codex,
 * everything but `[A-Za-z0-9_]` becomes `_`, so the name is also the identifier code mode scripts
 * call it by. `isTaken` reports names used by a different MCP tool: sanitizing can map two tools to
 * one name (`a-b` and `a_b`), which then get the hash suffix.
 */
export function createMcpToolName(
	server: string,
	tool: string,
	isTaken: (name: string) => boolean = () => false,
): string

## mcpNamespace  mcp/src/naming.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Namespace of a server's tools: `mcp__<server>` with `-` replaced by `_`, like the tool names. Server
 * names that differ only in `-` and `_` share a namespace, so a configuration must not have both.
 */
export function mcpNamespace(server: string): string

## createMcpAuthProvider  mcp/src/oauth/auth-provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Auth provider for MCP connections: sends the stored access token and refreshes it when it is about
 * to expire or after a 401. Throws `McpOAuthAuthorizationRequiredError` when the user has to sign in,
 * including when the server asks for more scope (`insufficient_scope`). `onChallenge` receives the
 * server's `WWW-Authenticate` challenge so sign-in can use its resource metadata URL and scope.
 * `settings` is only called when a refresh is needed, so a secret that fails to resolve fails the
 * refresh instead of the whole connection setup.
 *
 * Many servers rotate refresh tokens, so two refreshes with the same refresh token lose the grant.
 * Requests in this process share one refresh, and other processes are kept out by the store's
 * refresh lock, held from reading the tokens to saving new ones. Tokens that changed meanwhile
 * (another process refreshed them, or the user signed in) are used without refreshing.
 */
export function createMcpAuthProvider(
	options: Omit<McpOAuthClientOptions, "settings"> & {
		settings: () => McpOAuthSettings;
		onChallenge: (challenge: OAuthChallenge) => void;
		/**
		 * A redirect URI the application signs in with, such as its https callback route. Refreshing tokens
		 * from a sign-in with a Client ID Metadata Document needs a redirect URI the documents list; a
		 * refresh never redirects, so any listed one works. Default: the loopback redirect URI of `settings`.
		 */
		redirectUrl?: string;
	},
): McpAuthProvider

## McpAuthProvider  mcp/src/oauth/auth-provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** An `AuthProvider` that can say when its refreshes have finished. */
export interface McpAuthProvider extends AuthProvider {
	/** Resolves when no refresh is running, so shutdown does not drop rotated tokens before they are saved. */
	settled(): Promise<void>;
}

## OAuthCallbackServer  mcp/src/oauth/callback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export class OAuthCallbackServer {
	readonly redirectUrl: string
	static async listen(options: OAuthCallbackServerOptions = {}): Promise<OAuthCallbackServer>
	/**
	 * Wait for the authorization response with `state`. With `path`, a response on another path fails, so
	 * a server-specific redirect URI can tell authorization servers apart (RFC 9700 section 4.4.2.2).
	 */
	waitForCallback(state: string, path?: string): Promise<OAuthCallback>
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## OAuthCallbackServerOptions  mcp/src/oauth/callback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface OAuthCallbackServerOptions {
	/** Address to listen on. Default: `127.0.0.1`. */
	host?: string;
	/**
	 * Host name in `redirectUrl`, for example `localhost` for a client registered with it while
	 * listening on `127.0.0.1`. Default: `host`.
	 */
	redirectHost?: string;
	port?: number;
	path?: string;
	/** More paths that receive the callback, for example a server-specific path of a redirect URI. */
	extraPaths?: string[];
	timeoutMs?: number;
	/** Render the browser page as HTML. Default: a plain-text message. */
	renderPage?: (page: OAuthCallbackPage) => string;
}

## McpClientMetadataDocuments  mcp/src/oauth/client-settings.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * The Client ID Metadata Documents an application publishes: `<baseUrl>/client.json`, and for each MCP
 * server `<baseUrl>/<callback ID>/client.json`, whose redirect URIs carry the path `<path>/<callback ID>`.
 */
export interface McpClientMetadataDocuments {
	/** For example `https://pi.dev/oauth`. */
	baseUrl: string;
	/** Whether the documents list `redirectUrl`. Loopback redirect URIs match on any port (RFC 8252). */
	listsRedirectUrl(redirectUrl: string): boolean;
}

## McpOAuthClientOptions  mcp/src/oauth/client-settings.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** The OAuth client of one MCP server: where its state lives, its settings, and the application's identity. */
export interface McpOAuthClientOptions {
	serverUrl: string;
	store: McpOAuthServerStore;
	settings: McpOAuthSettings;
	/** `client_name` for dynamic client registration unless `settings.clientName` names another: the application. */
	clientName: string;
	/** Omitted: dynamic client registration only. */
	clientMetadataDocuments?: McpClientMetadataDocuments;
}

## McpOAuthServerStore  mcp/src/oauth/client-settings.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** State store of one MCP server, with a lock that keeps other processes from refreshing at the same time. */
export interface McpOAuthServerStore extends McpOAuthStateStore {
	/**
	 * Run `fn` while no other process refreshes the server's tokens. Not reentrant: `startMcpSignIn` and
	 * `createMcpAuthProvider` take it themselves, so never call them from `fn`. Throw
	 * `McpRefreshLockBusyError` when another process holds the lock for the whole wait: `startMcpSignIn`
	 * then goes to the browser step. Any other error fails the sign-in or refresh.
	 */
	withRefreshLock<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}

## McpOAuthSettings  mcp/src/oauth/client-settings.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Client settings of one MCP server, usually from the application's configuration. */
export interface McpOAuthSettings {
	/** Pre-registered client id. Without it, sign-in uses a Client ID Metadata Document or registers a client. */
	clientId?: string;
	/** Already resolved. */
	clientSecret?: string;
	/**
	 * Port of the loopback callback server, for clients registered with a fixed redirect URI. Without
	 * `callbackUrl`, the redirect URI is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`. Only `listenForLoopbackSignIn`
	 * and the redirect URI of refreshes use it; `startMcpSignIn` and `completeMcpSignIn` take theirs from
	 * the caller.
	 */
	callbackPort?: number;
	/**
	 * Loopback redirect URI registered for `clientId`, for example `http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback`.
	 * Without a port, the callback server listens on `callbackPort` or a free port, which is added to the
	 * URI (RFC 8252). Default: `http://127.0.0.1/callback`. Like `callbackPort`, only `listenForLoopbackSignIn`
	 * and refreshes use it.
	 */
	callbackUrl?: string;
	/** Scopes to request, separated by spaces. Default: the scopes the server advertises. */
	scope?: string;
	/** `client_name` for dynamic client registration. Default: the application's `clientName`. */
	clientName?: string;
	/**
	 * How to identify without `clientId`. `auto` (default): a Client ID Metadata Document when the
	 * authorization server supports them for public clients and the documents list the redirect URI,
	 * otherwise dynamic client registration; with `clientName`, always dynamic client registration.
	 * `cimd`: always the document, and sign-in fails without support. `dcr`: always dynamic client
	 * registration.
	 */
	clientRegistration?: "auto" | "dcr" | "cimd";
	/**
	 * Authorization server metadata document to use instead of discovery through the server, for servers
	 * that advertise a wrong authorization server or none. It is trusted as configured.
	 */
	authServerMetadataUrl?: URL;
}

## adaptOAuthProvider  mcp/src/oauth/flow.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Auth provider for `StreamableHttpTransport`. After a 401 it refreshes the tokens, or throws
 * `McpOAuthAuthorizationRequiredError` when the user has to authorize (again). Concurrent 401s share
 * one refresh, and a request whose token was already replaced is just retried: with rotating refresh
 * tokens, a second refresh with the old refresh token would fail and discard the new grant.
 */
export function adaptOAuthProvider(provider: OAuthClientProvider): AuthProvider

## OAuthClientProvider  mcp/src/oauth/flow.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface OAuthClientProvider {
	readonly redirectUrl: string | URL;
	readonly clientMetadata: OAuthClientMetadata;
	/**
	 * Client ID Metadata Document to identify as instead of registering dynamically, or `undefined` to
	 * register. Called when no client information is stored; the document is not stored. `metadata` is
	 * `undefined` when the authorization server has none; check `client_id_metadata_document_supported`.
	 */
	clientMetadataDocument?(metadata: AuthorizationServerMetadata | undefined): OAuthClientMetadataDocument | undefined;
	state?(): string | Promise<string>;
	clientInformation(): OAuthClientInformationMixed | undefined | Promise<OAuthClientInformationMixed | undefined>;
	saveClientInformation?(information: OAuthClientInformationMixed): void | Promise<void>;
	tokens(): OAuthTokens | undefined | Promise<OAuthTokens | undefined>;
	saveTokens(tokens: OAuthTokens): void | Promise<void>;
	redirectToAuthorization(url: URL): void | Promise<void>;
	saveCodeVerifier(verifier: string): void | Promise<void>;
	codeVerifier(): string | Promise<string>;
	addClientAuthentication?: AddClientAuthentication;
	invalidateCredentials?(kind: "all" | "client" | "tokens" | "verifier" | "discovery"): void | Promise<void>;
	saveDiscoveryState?(state: OAuthDiscoveryState): void | Promise<void>;
	discoveryState?(): OAuthDiscoveryState | undefined | Promise<OAuthDiscoveryState | undefined>;
}

## OAuthFlowOptions  mcp/src/oauth/flow.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface OAuthFlowOptions {
	serverUrl: string | URL;
	authorizationCode?: string;
	/** `iss` parameter of the authorization response that delivered `authorizationCode` (RFC 9207). */
	iss?: string;
	scope?: string;
	resourceMetadataUrl?: URL;
	/**
	 * Authorization server metadata document to use instead of discovery, for servers that advertise a
	 * wrong authorization server or none. It is trusted as configured. Must use https, except on loopback.
	 */
	authorizationServerMetadataUrl?: URL;
	fetch?: McpFetch;
	/** Aborts every request of the flow. Requests have no time limit of their own; combine with a timeout as needed. */
	signal?: AbortSignal;
	skipIssuerValidation?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Go straight to the authorization redirect instead of refreshing stored tokens, for example when the
	 * server asks for scopes the current grant lacks (a refresh keeps the old scope).
	 */
	skipRefresh?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Only refresh the stored tokens: return `REDIRECT` instead of registering a client or preparing an
	 * authorization request, so a pending authorization (its `state` and PKCE verifier) stays usable.
	 */
	refreshOnly?: boolean;
	/**
	 * With `authorizationCode`: the redirect URI the authorization request used. The exchange fails before
	 * sending the code when the flow would send another one (RFC 6749 section 4.1.3 requires the same).
	 */
	authorizationRedirectUrl?: string;
}

## OAuthFlowResult  mcp/src/oauth/flow.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type OAuthFlowResult = "AUTHORIZED" | "REDIRECT";

## stepUpScope  mcp/src/oauth/flow.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Scopes for a step-up authorization: the challenged scopes plus the ones granted so far, since a
 * challenge may list only the missing scopes and a token with just those would lose access the old
 * one had (SEP-2350). Without challenged scopes, `undefined` lets the flow pick its default.
 */
export function stepUpScope(granted: string | undefined, challenged: string | undefined): string | undefined

## listenForLoopbackSignIn  mcp/src/oauth/loopback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Listen for the authorization response of a sign-in on loopback, where `settings` say: `callbackUrl`
 * and `callbackPort`, else the port of the stored client's redirect URI (so that client stays valid) or
 * a free one. Pass the sign-in's `clientMetadataDocuments`, so the callback server also serves the
 * server-specific redirect URI. Close the callback server when the sign-in ends.
 */
export async function listenForLoopbackSignIn(options: {
	serverUrl: string;
	store: McpOAuthStateStore;
	settings: McpOAuthSettings;
	clientMetadataDocuments?: McpClientMetadataDocuments;
	/** Renders the browser page after the redirect. Default: plain text. */
	renderPage?: (page: OAuthCallbackPage) => string;
}): Promise<McpLoopbackCallback>

## McpLoopbackCallback  mcp/src/oauth/loopback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** A loopback callback server and the redirect URI it serves. */
export interface McpLoopbackCallback {
	callback: OAuthCallbackServer;
	/** Pass to `startMcpSignIn` and `completeMcpSignIn`. */
	redirectUrl: string;
}

## responseFromRedirectUrl  mcp/src/oauth/loopback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * The authorization response in a redirect URL the user pasted from the browser address bar. Fails when
 * the URL is not on the sign-in's redirect URI, carries another `state`, or reports an error.
 */
export function responseFromRedirectUrl(
	input: string,
	authorization: Pick<McpSignInRedirect, "state" | "redirectUrl">,
): McpAuthorizationResponse

## waitForLoopbackSignIn  mcp/src/oauth/loopback.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Wait for the authorization response on a loopback callback server, or for a redirect URL the user
 * pastes from the browser address bar, whichever comes first. Aborting `signal` stops the wait with
 * `McpSignInCancelledError`.
 */
export async function waitForLoopbackSignIn(options: {
	callback: OAuthCallbackServer;
	/** The `redirect` result of `startMcpSignIn`. */
	authorization: McpSignInRedirect;
	/**
	 * Ask for the redirect URL, for when the browser cannot reach the loopback callback (for example over
	 * SSH). Aborted once the callback arrives or the sign-in is cancelled. Resolving to `undefined` or an
	 * empty string cancels the sign-in.
	 */
	promptForRedirectUrl?: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<string | undefined>;
	signal?: AbortSignal;
}): Promise<McpAuthorizationResponse>

## McpOAuthProvider  mcp/src/oauth/provider.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Default stateful provider for one exact MCP server URL. Applications inject durable storage if needed. */
export class McpOAuthProvider implements OAuthClientProvider {
	readonly redirectUrl: string
	readonly clientMetadata: OAuthClientMetadata
	readonly clientMetadataDocument?: (
		metadata: AuthorizationServerMetadata | undefined,
	) => OAuthClientMetadataDocument | undefined
	constructor(options: McpOAuthProviderOptions)
	async state(): Promise<string>
	async clientInformation(): Promise<OAuthClientInformationMixed | undefined>
	async saveClientInformation(information: OAuthClientInformationMixed): Promise<void>
	async tokens(): Promise<OAuthTokens | undefined>
	async saveTokens(tokens: OAuthTokens): Promise<void>
	async redirectToAuthorization(url: URL): Promise<void>
	async saveCodeVerifier(verifier: string): Promise<void>
	async codeVerifier(): Promise<string>
	async invalidateCredentials(kind: "all" | "client" | "tokens" | "verifier" | "discovery"): Promise<void>
	async saveDiscoveryState(discovery: OAuthDiscoveryState): Promise<void>
	async discoveryState(): Promise<OAuthDiscoveryState | undefined>
}

		metadata: AuthorizationServerMetadata | undefined,
	) => OAuthClientMetadataDocument | undefined;
	clientId?: string;

	onRedirect(url: URL): void | Promise<void>;
}

## completeMcpSignIn  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Second half of a sign-in: exchanges the authorization code of `response` and saves the tokens. Pass
 * the options given to `startMcpSignIn`, including its `redirectUrl` (not `authorization.redirectUrl`).
 * Fails when the response carries another `state`, when another sign-in started with the store since, or
 * when the exchange would use another redirect URI than the authorization request (the options changed).
 * A redirect URL the user pasted goes through `responseFromRedirectUrl` first, which checks its path.
 */
export async function completeMcpSignIn(
	options: McpSignInOptions & {
		/** The `redirect` result of `startMcpSignIn`. */
		authorization: McpSignInRedirect;
		response: McpAuthorizationResponse;
	},
): Promise<void>

## McpAuthorizationResponse  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** An authorization response: from a callback server, a callback route, or `responseFromRedirectUrl`. */
export type McpAuthorizationResponse = OAuthCallback;

## McpSignInCancelledError  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** The user or the application cancelled a sign-in (its `signal` was aborted, or the user gave up). */
export class McpSignInCancelledError extends Error {
	constructor()
}

## McpSignInOptions  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Options of both halves of a sign-in. Pass the same values to `startMcpSignIn` and `completeMcpSignIn`. */
export interface McpSignInOptions extends McpOAuthClientOptions {
	/**
	 * Redirect URI chosen by the caller: a loopback one (`listenForLoopbackSignIn`) or an https callback
	 * route of the application. Pass the same one to both halves: the authorization request may use a
	 * variant specific to the MCP server (`McpSignInRedirect.redirectUrl`), which the flow derives from it.
	 */
	redirectUrl: string;
	/** The server's challenge that asked for the sign-in; its resource metadata URL and scope apply. */
	challenge?: OAuthChallenge;
	/**
	 * Aborting stops the sign-in at once with `McpSignInCancelledError`, also while `startMcpSignIn` waits
	 * for the store's refresh lock. A refresh already sent still completes and saves its tokens.
	 */
	signal?: AbortSignal;
}

## McpSignInRedirect  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** The browser step of a sign-in, from `startMcpSignIn`. Plain data, so an application can persist it. */
export interface McpSignInRedirect {
	kind: "redirect";
	/** Open in the user's browser. */
	authorizationUrl: string;
	/** The redirect URI of the authorization request; the authorization response must arrive on it. */
	redirectUrl: string;
	/** The `state` parameter the authorization response must carry. */
	state: string;
	/** The scope requested, if any. Saved with the tokens when the token response names none. */
	scope?: string;
}

## McpSignInStart  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Result of `startMcpSignIn`: signed in by refreshing the stored tokens, or the browser step. */
export type McpSignInStart = { kind: "authorized" } | McpSignInRedirect;

## startMcpSignIn  mcp/src/oauth/sign-in.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * First half of a sign-in. Without a step-up (`insufficient_scope`), it first tries to refresh the stored
 * tokens with the stored client, whatever `redirectUrl` is (`authorized`). The refresh takes the store's
 * refresh lock, so never call this while holding it; when another process holds the lock for the whole
 * wait (`McpRefreshLockBusyError`), the refresh is skipped, and any other failure of the lock fails the
 * sign-in. Otherwise it prepares the browser step (`redirect`): a fresh `state`, and a stored client that
 * cannot use `redirectUrl` is dropped with its tokens. Requests to the authorization server are
 * time-limited.
 */
export async function startMcpSignIn(options: McpSignInOptions): Promise<McpSignInStart>

/**
 * Keep model-facing text within {@link MCP_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES}. Longer text becomes one text block in

## toLlmContent  mcp/src/protocol/content.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Convert a tool result to text and image content for a model. Text and images pass through,
 * embedded text resources become text, embedded image resources become images, and other blocks
 * (audio, resource links, binary resources) become a short text placeholder. A result without
 * content blocks but with `structuredContent` becomes its JSON, since servers should, but do not
 * always, mirror structured results as text.
 */
export function toLlmContent(result: Pick<CallToolResult, "content" | "structuredContent">): LlmContent[]

/** A family of resources, addressed by an RFC 6570 URI template, from `resources/templates/list`. */
export interface ResourceTemplate {
	uriTemplate: string;
	name: string;
	title?: string;
	description?: string;
	mimeType?: string;
	annotations?: ContentAnnotations;
	_meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

## SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS  mcp/src/protocol/types.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Versions the client accepts from a server. Servers that do not support the requested version answer
 * with their own latest one, so older versions stay accepted for servers built on older SDKs.
 */
export const SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = [LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, "2025-06-18", "2025-03-26", "2024-11-05"] as const

## SupportedProtocolVersion  mcp/src/protocol/types.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type SupportedProtocolVersion = (typeof SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS)[number];

## createMcpResultSchema  mcp/src/result-schema.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * Output schema of an MCP tool: the `CallToolResult` programs receive (without `_meta`, which callers drop), with the
 * tool's own output schema as `structuredContent`. Without one, structured content may be any JSON value.
 */
export function createMcpResultSchema(
	structuredContentSchema: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
): Record<string, unknown>

export function createInMemoryTransportPair(): { client: InMemoryTransport; server: InMemoryTransport }

## InMemoryTransport  mcp/src/transports/in-memory.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export class InMemoryTransport extends TransportEvents implements McpTransport {
	connectPeer(peer: InMemoryTransport): void
	async start(): Promise<void>
	async send(message: JsonRpcMessage): Promise<void>
	async close(): Promise<void>
	/** Exposed so tests can simulate transport-level failures. */
	override emitError(error: unknown): void
}

## McpPipe  mcp/src/transports/pipe.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** A running program's stdio, as `@earendil-works/pi-env`'s `RemoteProcess` provides it. */
export interface McpPipe {
	write(data: Uint8Array | string): void;
	closeStdin(): void;
	/** Kill the program (and what it started). The pipe owns cleaning up what the program started. */
	close(): void;
	/** Settles when the program has ended, whatever the reason; it must also settle after `close()`. */
	readonly exited: Promise<unknown>;
}

## McpPipeHandlers  mcp/src/transports/pipe.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/** Handlers `PipeTransportOptions.open` connects to the program's output. */
export interface McpPipeHandlers {
	onStdout(bytes: Uint8Array): void;
	onStderr(bytes: Uint8Array): void;
}

## PipeTransport  mcp/src/transports/pipe.ts
used by: mcp-effect
/**
 * MCP's stdio transport over a program that something else runs, for example on another machine through pi-env.
 * The transport closes when the program ends; a rejected `exited` that `close()` did not cause is reported as an
 * error first.
 */
export class PipeTransport extends TransportEvents implements McpTransport {
	readonly options: Readonly<PipeTransportOptions>
	constructor(options: PipeTransportOptions)
	/** The last `maxStderrBytes` (default 64 KiB) of the program's stderr. */
	get stderr(): string
	async start(): Promise<void>
	async send(message: JsonRpcMessage): Promise<void>
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## PipeTransportOptions  mcp/src/transports/pipe.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface PipeTransportOptions {
	/** Start the program; `onStdout`/`onStderr` receive its output from then on. */
	open(handlers: McpPipeHandlers): Promise<McpPipe>;
	maxMessageBytes?: number;
	maxStderrBytes?: number;
	onStderr?: (chunk: string) => void;
	/** After closing stdin, how long the program may take to exit before `close()` kills it. Default 2000. */
	closeTimeoutMs?: number;
}

## StdioTransport  mcp/src/transports/stdio.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export class StdioTransport extends TransportEvents implements McpTransport {
	readonly options: Readonly<StdioTransportOptions>
	constructor(options: StdioTransportOptions)
	get pid(): number | undefined
	get stderr(): string
	async start(): Promise<void>
	async send(message: JsonRpcMessage): Promise<void>
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## StdioTransportOptions  mcp/src/transports/stdio.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface StdioTransportOptions {
	command: string;
	args?: readonly string[];
	cwd?: string;
	env?: Record<string, string>;
	inheritEnv?: boolean;
	stderr?: "pipe" | "inherit";
	onStderr?: (chunk: string) => void;
	maxMessageBytes?: number;
	maxStderrBytes?: number;
	/** Time to wait for the server to exit after SIGTERM before sending SIGKILL. Default: 2000. */
	closeTimeoutMs?: number;
}

## StreamableHttpReconnectOptions  mcp/src/transports/streamable-http.ts
used by: mcp-effect via StreamableHttpTransportOptions
export interface StreamableHttpReconnectOptions {
	/** Delay before the first reconnection attempt, unless the server sent a `retry` field. Default: 1000. */
	initialDelayMs?: number;
	/** Upper bound for the exponential backoff. Default: 30000. */
	maxDelayMs?: number;
	/** Consecutive failed attempts before giving up on a stream. Default: 5. */
	maxRetries?: number;
}

## StreamableHttpTransport  mcp/src/transports/streamable-http.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export class StreamableHttpTransport extends TransportEvents implements McpTransport {
	readonly url: URL
	readonly options: Readonly<StreamableHttpTransportOptions>
	constructor(options: StreamableHttpTransportOptions)
	get sessionId(): string | undefined
	async start(): Promise<void>
	setProtocolVersion(version: string): void
	async send(message: JsonRpcMessage, { signal }: McpTransportSendOptions = {}): Promise<void>
	async close(): Promise<void>
}

## StreamableHttpTransportOptions  mcp/src/transports/streamable-http.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface StreamableHttpTransportOptions {
	url: string | URL;
	headers?: Record<string, string>;
	fetch?: McpFetch;
	/** Open the server-to-client GET stream after initialization. Default: true. */
	openGetStream?: boolean;
	maxMessageBytes?: number;
	authProvider?: AuthProvider;
	/** Reconnection of dropped SSE streams (the GET stream, and response streams that carry event IDs). */
	reconnect?: StreamableHttpReconnectOptions;
}

## McpTransport  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface McpTransport {
	start(): Promise<void>;
	send(message: JsonRpcMessage, options?: McpTransportSendOptions): Promise<void>;
	close(): Promise<void>;
	onMessage(listener: McpTransportMessageListener): () => void;
	onError(listener: McpTransportErrorListener): () => void;
	onClose(listener: McpTransportCloseListener): () => void;
	setProtocolVersion?(version: string): void;
}

## McpTransportCloseListener  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type McpTransportCloseListener = () => void;

## McpTransportErrorListener  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type McpTransportErrorListener = (error: Error) => void;

## McpTransportMessageListener  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export type McpTransportMessageListener = (message: JsonRpcMessage) => void;

## McpTransportSendOptions  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect
export interface McpTransportSendOptions {
	/**
	 * Aborted once the sender no longer waits for a reply (the request was cancelled, timed out, answered,
	 * or the client closed). A transport must not dispatch the message after that, for example when
	 * retrying it after an authorization refresh. It does not undo a message already dispatched.
	 */
	signal?: AbortSignal;
}

## TransportEvents  mcp/src/transports/transport.ts
used by: mcp-effect via InMemoryTransport
/** Listener bookkeeping shared by transports. `emitClose` fires at most once per transport. */
export abstract class TransportEvents {
	onMessage(listener: McpTransportMessageListener): () => void
	onError(listener: McpTransportErrorListener): () => void
	onClose(listener: McpTransportCloseListener): () => void
}
